hints.title: Exact Aspect Ratio Representation
hints.text: Two rectangles have equivalent aspect ratios when width divided by height equals the other rectangle ratio.

hints.title: Greatest Common Divisor Reduction
hints.text: Avoid floating point precision issues by dividing both width and height by their greatest common divisor.

hints.title: Combinatorial Pair Counting
hints.text: Store normalized width-height coordinate pairs in a frequency map and sum count times count minus one divided by two.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def interchangeableRectangles(self, rectangles: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        freq = defaultdict(int)
        for w, h in rectangles:
            g = math.gcd(w, h)
            freq[(w // g, h // g)] += 1
        ans = 0
        for cnt in freq.values():
            ans += cnt * (cnt - 1) // 2
        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(N log(min(W, H))) where N is the number of rectangles and log steps calculate the greatest common divisor
complexity.space: O(N) storing distinct canonical aspect ratios in a hash map
complexity.notes: Canonical integer pairs prevent rounding errors common in floating-point ratios.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pairwise double loop takes O(N^2) time, which exceeds the time limit for one hundred thousand rectangles.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hashing reduced fractions reduces quadratic search to linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize fractional equality via greatest common divisor and apply arithmetic combinations.
